questions.question:
Station settings for the tide gauges are kept as ConfigMaps in namespace `tides`.

1. Create a ConfigMap named `gauge-config` from the file `/home/candidate/exam/q1/gauge.properties`. The whole file must be stored under the single key `station.conf`.
2. Add the labels `tier=gauge` and `region=west` to `gauge-config`.
3. Write the names of all ConfigMaps in namespace `tides` that match the label selector `tier=gauge,status!=retired` to `/home/candidate/exam/q1/active-gauges.txt`: names only (no `configmap/` prefix), sorted alphabetically, one per line.

verification.description: ConfigMap gauge-config stores gauge.properties under the single key station.conf
gauge-config is labelled tier=gauge and region=west
active-gauges.txt lists the ConfigMaps matching tier=gauge,status!=retired, sorted, one per line

questions.question:
The Deployment `crane` in namespace `quayside` has gone through several rollouts. Its most recent update broke it: the new pods can never start and the rollout is stuck.

1. Roll `crane` back to the **last revision that was working** (the revision right before the broken update). Do not delete or recreate the Deployment.
2. Make sure the rollback completes and all `3` replicas are updated and ready.
3. Write the revision number the Deployment is running now, i.e. the value of its `deployment.kubernetes.io/revision` annotation after the rollback, to `/home/candidate/exam/q2/revision.txt` (only the number).

verification.description: Deployment crane runs the last working template (nginx:1.25 with LIFT_MODE=tandem)
Rollback completed: 3/3 replicas updated and ready, no stuck pods left
revision.txt contains the Deployment's active revision number after the rollback

questions.question:
A customs clearance app in namespace `customs` needs broker credentials.

1. Create a generic Secret named `broker-creds` with two keys: `api-token` = `tk-7731-harbor` and `broker-id` = `HL-0042`.
2. Create a Pod named `declarations` with a single container named `clerk` (image `nginx:1.25`) that:
   - mounts the **whole** Secret `broker-creds` (every key, no `items` list) as a volume at `/etc/customs/creds`, with the volume mount set to `readOnly: true`
   - exposes the Secret key `broker-id` as the environment variable `CUSTOMS_BROKER_ID` using `secretKeyRef` (not a literal value)

The Pod must be `Running`.

verification.description: Secret broker-creds (Opaque) has api-token=tk-7731-harbor and broker-id=HL-0042
Whole secret mounted at /etc/customs/creds in container clerk (both key files readable)
The secret volume mount is readOnly: true
CUSTOMS_BROKER_ID comes from secretKeyRef broker-creds/broker-id and printenv shows HL-0042

questions.question:
The harbor signal team wants a quick smoke test of its new status page.

In namespace `signal`:

1. Create a Pod named `foghorn` (image `nginx:1.25`) with the label `app=foghorn`.
2. Create a Service named `foghorn-svc` of type `ClusterIP` that selects `app=foghorn` and listens on port `8080`, forwarding to container port `80`.
3. From a temporary Pod (image `busybox:1.36`) in namespace `signal` that is removed once it finishes, request `http://foghorn-svc:8080/` and save the response body to `/home/candidate/exam/q4/response.html`.
4. After that request, save the logs of the `foghorn` Pod to `/home/candidate/exam/q4/foghorn.log`.

verification.description: Pod foghorn runs nginx:1.25 with label app=foghorn
Service foghorn-svc is ClusterIP, port 8080 -> targetPort 80, with the foghorn Pod as endpoint
response.html contains the nginx welcome page
foghorn.log contains an nginx GET access log line

questions.question:
In namespace `beacon`:

1. Create a Pod named `lamp-keeper` using image `busybox:1.36`, with the label `tier=signal` and the environment variable `BEAM_COLOR=amber`. Its container must run the command `sh -c 'while true; do echo "beam=$BEAM_COLOR"; sleep 5; done'`.
2. Write a **single-line** `kubectl` command to `/home/candidate/exam/q5/phase.sh` that uses `jsonpath` output to print **only** the status phase of Pod `lamp-keeper` (e.g. `Running`). The file will be run with `bash`; the command must work regardless of the current namespace and print nothing else (other pods exist in `beacon`).

verification.description: Pod lamp-keeper is Running with image busybox:1.36 and label tier=signal
BEAM_COLOR=amber is set and the container logs show beam=amber
phase.sh is a one-line kubectl jsonpath command that prints only Running

questions.question:
In namespace `lighthouse`, the Deployment `lamp-driver` (2 replicas) sets the environment variable `LAMP_ROTATION` from key `rotation` of the ConfigMap `lamp-config`. Operations wants the lamp to rotate faster.

1. Change the value of key `rotation` in ConfigMap `lamp-config` to `fast`. Leave the other keys of the ConfigMap unchanged.
2. Make sure the running Pods of `lamp-driver` actually use the new value. The Deployment must keep reading `LAMP_ROTATION` from the ConfigMap key (do not hard-code the value) and must end up with 2 ready, up-to-date replicas.
3. Annotate the ConfigMap `lamp-config` with `harbor-logistics.io/change-ticket=HL-4471`.

verification.description: ConfigMap lamp-config has rotation=fast and color unchanged
lamp-driver still reads LAMP_ROTATION from the ConfigMap, 2 ready replicas, and every running Pod has LAMP_ROTATION=fast
ConfigMap lamp-config is annotated harbor-logistics.io/change-ticket=HL-4471

questions.question:
The finance team needs a nightly ledger reconciliation in namespace `ledger`.

Create a CronJob named `reconcile` with:
- schedule `15 2 * * *`
- `successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 5` and `failedJobsHistoryLimit: 2`
- Pod `restartPolicy: Never` and one container named `reconciler`, image `busybox:1.36`, command `["sh", "-c", "echo ledger-ok uid=$(id -u)"]`
- Pod-level securityContext `runAsUser: 2500` and `runAsNonRoot: true`
- container-level securityContext `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`

Then, without waiting for the schedule, create a one-off Job named `reconcile-manual-01` from the CronJob `reconcile`. The Job must complete successfully.

verification.description: CronJob reconcile: schedule 15 2 * * *, history limits 5/2, restartPolicy Never, image busybox:1.36
Pod runs as uid 2500 with runAsNonRoot=true and readOnlyRootFilesystem=true
Job reconcile-manual-01 was created from (is owned by) CronJob reconcile
Job reconcile-manual-01 succeeded and its log shows uid=2500

questions.question:
A Kustomize base for the `weighbridge` app is in `/home/candidate/exam/q8/base`: a Deployment `weighbridge` (3 replicas, `nginx:1.25`) and a Service `weighbridge` selecting `app: weighbridge`, both in namespace `tally`. Do not modify the base.

1. Create a canary overlay at `/home/candidate/exam/q8/overlays/canary/kustomization.yaml` that uses `../../base` as its resource and renders **exactly one object**: a Deployment named `weighbridge-canary` (name suffix `-canary`) with `1` replica and image `nginx:1.26`, whose pods carry the extra label `track: canary` while keeping `app: weighbridge`, so the existing Service also routes to them. The overlay must not render a Service.
2. Apply the base and the canary overlay with `kubectl apply -k`.

When done, the Service `weighbridge` (selector unchanged) must have 4 ready endpoints: 3 stable pods and 1 canary pod.

verification.description: Deployment weighbridge has 3 ready replicas of nginx:1.25
Deployment weighbridge-canary has 1 ready nginx:1.26 replica labelled app=weighbridge, track=canary
Service weighbridge (selector app=weighbridge) has 4 endpoints including 1 canary pod
overlays/canary uses ../../base and renders only Deployment weighbridge-canary; base unchanged

questions.question:
In namespace `yard` the Deployment `forklift` is already running. The manifest `/home/candidate/exam/q9/forklift-hpa.yaml` defines a HorizontalPodAutoscaler for it, but it uses `autoscaling/v2beta2`, an API version that is no longer served, so `kubectl apply` fails.

Edit the file in place so that it:
- uses `apiVersion: autoscaling/v2`
- keeps the name `forklift-hpa` and the target Deployment `forklift`
- sets `minReplicas: 2`, `maxReplicas: 5` and a CPU target of type `Utilization` with `averageUtilization: 60`

Apply the file. Once applied, the HPA scales `forklift` up to its new minimum on its own; make sure `forklift` ends up with at least 2 ready replicas.

verification.description: forklift-hpa.yaml uses autoscaling/v2 with min 2, max 5, cpu Utilization 60
Live HPA forklift-hpa targets Deployment forklift with min 2, max 5, cpu Utilization 60
Deployment forklift has at least 2 ready replicas

questions.question:
A local Helm chart is available at `/home/candidate/exam/q10/dockyard`. Two releases of it are installed in namespace `berth`: `tugboat` and `pilot-legacy`.

1. Upgrade release `tugboat` with the same chart so that it runs `2` replicas (chart value `replicaCount`) and its pods get the annotation `crew: night-shift` (chart value `podAnnotations.crew`). The values already set on the release (such as its existing pod annotation) must be preserved.
2. Uninstall the release `pilot-legacy`.
3. Install a new release named `harbormaster` from the same chart into namespace `berth`, with `service.type` set to `NodePort`.

verification.description: tugboat upgraded (deployed, revision >= 2) with replicaCount=2 and 2 ready pods
tugboat pods annotated crew=night-shift and the existing owner=berth-ops value is kept
Release pilot-legacy and its resources are removed
Release harbormaster (chart dockyard) is deployed in berth with a NodePort Service

questions.question:
The cargo team keeps its manifest ledger on node-local storage that must be provisioned by hand.

1. Create a PersistentVolume named `ledger-pv` with capacity `200Mi`, access mode `ReadWriteOnce` (only), `storageClassName: manual` and a `hostPath` volume at `/tmp/cargo-ledger` (hostPath type `DirectoryOrCreate`).
2. In namespace `cargo`, create a PersistentVolumeClaim named `ledger-claim` with `storageClassName: manual`, access mode `ReadWriteOnce` and a request of `200Mi`. It must be `Bound` to `ledger-pv`.
3. In namespace `cargo`, create a Pod named `ledger-writer` (image `busybox:1.36`) that mounts `ledger-claim` at `/ledger`, writes the text `manifest=sealed` to the file `/ledger/entry.txt` and then keeps running (for example with `sleep 86400`).

verification.description: PV ledger-pv: storageClassName manual, 200Mi, ReadWriteOnce, hostPath /tmp/cargo-ledger
PVC ledger-claim (class manual, RWO) is Bound to ledger-pv
Pod ledger-writer (busybox:1.36) is Running and mounts ledger-claim at /ledger
/ledger/entry.txt in ledger-writer contains manifest=sealed

questions.question:
In namespace `manifest`, the ClusterIP Service `manifest-api` should expose the pods of Deployment `manifest-api` on port `8080`, but it has no endpoints and every request to it fails.

Fix the **Service** in place (keep its name, type `ClusterIP` and port `8080`) so that it selects the pods of Deployment `manifest-api` and forwards traffic to the container port declared by the Deployment's nginx container. Do not modify or recreate the Deployment.

When done, the Service must list both `manifest-api` pods as endpoints.

verification.description: Service selector matches the (unchanged) manifest-api pod labels
Service is still ClusterIP and port 8080 targets container port 80 (http)
Endpoints list both manifest-api pods on port 80

questions.question:
Namespace `pier` runs three Pods: `gate-ui` (label `tier=frontend`), `dispatch-api` (label `tier=backend`) and `berth-db` (label `tier=db`, Redis listening on TCP port `6379`). At the moment every Pod can connect to `berth-db`.

Create a NetworkPolicy named `berth-db-access` in namespace `pier` that:

- applies only to Pods with the label `tier=db`
- has `policyTypes` set to `Ingress` only (egress must not be restricted)
- in a single ingress rule, allows traffic only from Pods with the label `tier=backend` in namespace `pier`, and only on TCP port `6379`

Do not modify the existing Pods.

verification.description: berth-db-access selects the tier=db Pod and no other Pod
policyTypes is exactly [Ingress]
Single ingress rule whose only peer is a podSelector for tier=backend in namespace pier
Ingress rule allows only TCP port 6379

questions.question:
In namespace `gatehouse`, create a Deployment named `boom-gate` with `3` replicas. Its only container, named `controller`, uses image `busybox:1.36` and runs:

`sh -c 'sleep 15; touch /tmp/gate-open; while true; do sleep 3600; done'`

The gate needs about 15 seconds to warm up and must not receive traffic before `/tmp/gate-open` exists. Add a **readiness probe** to the container that executes `cat /tmp/gate-open`, with `initialDelaySeconds: 5` and `periodSeconds: 5`.

Make sure all 3 replicas become ready.

verification.description: boom-gate has 3 replicas; container controller (busybox:1.36) runs the given command
exec readinessProbe on /tmp/gate-open with initialDelaySeconds=5 and periodSeconds=5
All 3 boom-gate replicas are updated, ready and available

questions.question:
In namespace `winch` the Deployment `hoist-controller` runs a container `hoist` that appends a line every 3 seconds to `/var/log/hoist/cycles.log` on an `emptyDir` volume named `hoist-logs`, so nothing shows up in `kubectl logs`. Its manifest is at `/home/candidate/exam/q15/hoist-controller.yaml`.

Add a logging sidecar to the Deployment as an additional regular container (under `containers`, not `initContainers`):
- name `log-tail`, image `busybox:1.36`
- mounts the existing `hoist-logs` volume at `/var/log/hoist`
- command `["sh", "-c", "tail -n +1 -F /var/log/hoist/cycles.log"]`

Leave the `hoist` container unchanged. After the rollout, `kubectl logs` for the `log-tail` container of the running Pod must show the `hoist cycle complete` lines.

verification.description: Deployment hoist-controller has containers hoist and log-tail (busybox:1.36)
log-tail mounts the hoist-logs emptyDir at /var/log/hoist, shared with hoist
kubectl logs -c log-tail of the running pod shows the hoist cycle lines

questions.question:
Namespace `wharf` needs guard-rails before the loading teams start deploying there. Do the following in namespace `wharf`, in this order:

1. Create a LimitRange named `crate-defaults` that, for type `Container`, sets default **requests** of cpu `50m` and memory `64Mi` and default **limits** of cpu `100m` and memory `128Mi`.
2. Create a ResourceQuota named `wharf-quota` with the hard limits `pods=4`, `requests.cpu=400m` and `limits.memory=512Mi`.
3. Create a Pod named `forklift` (image `nginx:1.25`) **without** a `resources` section. It must get all of its requests and limits from the LimitRange and be `Running`.

verification.description: LimitRange crate-defaults: Container defaultRequest 50m/64Mi and default 100m/128Mi
ResourceQuota wharf-quota: pods=4, requests.cpu=400m, limits.memory=512Mi
Pod forklift (nginx:1.25) is Running with requests 50m/64Mi and limits 100m/128Mi
forklift's requests and limits were injected by the LimitRange (none set in the Pod spec)

questions.question:
Namespace `dockhands` has six Pods labelled with a `role` (`stevedore`, `lasher` or `clerk`). Change their metadata in place (do not delete or recreate any Pod):

1. Add the label `shift=night` to every Pod with `role=stevedore`. No other Pod may have `shift=night`.
2. Set the annotation `safety.example.com/certified=rigging-l2` on every Pod with `role=lasher` (one of them already carries an outdated value). No other Pod may carry this annotation.
3. Remove the label `onboarding` from every Pod in the namespace that has it.

verification.description: All role=stevedore pods, and only those, have shift=night
All role=lasher pods, and only those, have safety.example.com/certified=rigging-l2
All 6 pods still exist and none carries the onboarding label
